job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

passage: In India, the democratic process relies on the active participation of all adult citizens, regardless of their education or property ownership. Every eligible citizen has the right to vote, and this act is a voluntary exercise of their democratic duty, not a legal obligation punishable by law. When a voter enters the polling station, they use an Electronic Voting Machine (EVM) to cast their ballot. Contrary to popular myths, EVMs are standalone machines that are not connected to the internet or any external network, ensuring they cannot be hacked remotely. After pressing the button for their chosen candidate, a VVPAT machine prints a slip showing the name and symbol of the candidate selected. This slip is visible to the voter for seven seconds behind a glass window before it drops into a sealed box, serving as a record for the Election Commission, not as a receipt for the voter to take home. Furthermore, the Election Commission functions as an independent constitutional body, completely separate from the ruling government or the Prime Minister's office. Finally, voters must remember that they are electing a representative for their local constituency, not directly voting for the Prime Minister. The system is designed to ensure that the process remains transparent, secure, and accessible to every citizen.

items.evidence: In India, the democratic process relies on the active participation of all adult citizens, regardless of their education or property ownership.
items.q: Meena is an adult citizen who never went to school and owns no land. What is true about her vote?
options: She can vote, just like every adult citizen
She can vote only after she learns to read
She can vote only if her family owns land
She can vote, but is fined if she skips
items.explain: All adult citizens take part in voting, whatever their education or property.

wrong.why: thinks only educated people can vote
links the right to vote with owning property
thinks voting is compulsory and punished

items.evidence: Every eligible citizen has the right to vote, and this act is a voluntary exercise of their democratic duty, not a legal obligation punishable by law.
items.q: Raju is eligible but stays at home on polling day. What happens to him under the law?
options: He faces no penalty, since it is his choice
He must pay a fine for not voting
He loses his right to vote next time
He is jailed under the Code of Conduct
items.explain: Voting is voluntary, not a legal obligation, so not voting is not punished by law.

wrong.why: thinks voting is compulsory and fined
thinks missing a vote takes the right away
thinks the Code of Conduct sends people to jail

items.evidence: Contrary to popular myths, EVMs are standalone machines that are not connected to the internet or any external network, ensuring they cannot be hacked remotely.
items.q: Why can't a hacker in another city change the votes stored in an EVM?
options: It works alone with no network connection
It uses a secret, protected Wi-Fi password
Its VVPAT slip blocks changes from outside
Its commission is independent of the government
items.explain: EVMs are standalone and not linked to the internet or any network, so remote hacking is impossible.

wrong.why: picks a nearby detail that is not the reason
picks a true fact that does not explain security

items.evidence: This slip is visible to the voter for seven seconds behind a glass window before it drops into a sealed box, serving as a record for the Election Commission, not as a receipt for the voter to take home.
items.q: Asha wants to keep her VVPAT slip as proof of her vote. What happens to the slip?
options: The slip shows briefly, then falls into a sealed box
The slip is handed to her to take home
The slip goes to an officer to note her choice
The slip is not printed; only the EVM records
items.explain: The slip shows for seven seconds, then drops into a sealed box as the Commission's record.

wrong.why: thinks the slip is a receipt to take home
thinks officials see each person's vote
thinks the EVM is one box with no slip

items.evidence: Finally, voters must remember that they are electing a representative for their local constituency, not directly voting for the Prime Minister.
items.q: When Priya presses a button on the EVM, whom is she actually choosing?
options: A representative for her local constituency
The Prime Minister directly, for the country
An officer of the Election Commission
The ruling party's leader for her state
items.explain: Voters elect a representative for their local constituency, not the Prime Minister directly.

wrong.why: thinks voters directly elect the Prime Minister
picks another body named in the passage
thinks the vote is for a party leader
